exposure: Duration of active second stage of labor
outcome: High umbilical arterial lactate levels (>=5.80 mmol/L)
cohort: The study included 7723 women and their singleton newborns (7301 spontaneous vaginal and 422 elective cesareans) from Kuopio University Hospital, Finland, with 6541 healthy term neonates specifically evaluated for high lactate levels after vaginal delivery.
finding: Umbilical arterial lactate levels were significantly lower after elective cesarean delivery compared to vaginal delivery, and higher lactate values after vaginal birth were independently associated with a longer duration of the active second stage of labor, longer duration of ruptured fetal membranes, higher gestational age at birth, nulliparity, maternal infection, and short maternal stature.
mod_finding: The mean umbilical arterial lactate level was significantly lower after elective cesarean delivery (2.42 mmol/l) compared to vaginal delivery (3.56 mmol/l), and high levels after vaginal birth reflect physiological stress and subclinical transient asphyxia.
